headline: Highest risk is medium: Plane can ingest files and broad egress while Plano is an out-of-process OpenAI-compatible gateway, creating plausible leakage and instruction-confusion paths, but no direct shared-channel evidence is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plane can ingest file uploads and touches files, while Plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint and broad network egress. That creates a plausible path where Plane-produced content is forwarded into Plano and later treated as instructions. No shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Plane file uploads are forwarded into Plano prompts without sanitization
IF Plano downstream tool prompts are built from Plane-generated text
mitigations: Disable automatic forwarding of Plane file contents into Plano prompts
Add a fixed system prompt separator before any Plane-derived text
Require manual review for any content copied from Plane into Plano
Log and flag any prompt segment containing file-upload text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between Plane and Plano

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches files, notes, issues, and roadmaps, and supports file uploads; Plano is an out-of-process gateway with broad egress. Even without a shared workspace, forwarding Plane data through Plano can leak sensitive work products to a third party. The pairwise path is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Plane uploads or notes are sent through Plano to external model APIs
IF shared credentials or logs capture Plane file contents in Plano traffic
mitigations: Restrict Plane uploads to non-sensitive files
Route Plano traffic through a redaction proxy
Turn off verbose request logging in Plano
Separate credentials used by Plane and Plano
requires-engineering: enforce data-class allowlists at the gateway

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plane cannot write its filesystem, while Plano does not spawn subprocesses and has no filesystem write capability listed. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable-resource writes, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty is low because the relevant write surfaces are absent in both profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to mutate the same external resource through an unlisted integration
mitigations: Keep Plane and Plano on separate service accounts
Avoid pointing both at the same writable config directory
Review any shared API credentials before deployment
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking for shared backends

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane produces issues, tasks, roadmaps, and notes, which Plano could plausibly consume as upstream context. Plano’s gateway role makes it likely to relay or transform that output, so a mistaken Plane artifact could cascade into downstream actions or responses. No verification step is documented, but the action authority is not explicit enough for high.
conditions: IF Plano uses Plane-generated issues or notes as authoritative prompt context
IF downstream consumers act on Plano outputs without independent verification
mitigations: Insert a human review step before Plano consumes Plane output
Require citations or source links for Plane-derived facts
Mark Plane output as untrusted in Plano prompts
Add regression tests for malformed Plane artifacts
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Plane’s docs indicate self-hosted deployment and file uploads, while Plano is an OpenAI-compatible gateway with broad egress. That combination can create compliance friction around residency and retention if sensitive Plane data is routed through Plano, but the profiles do not document a specific regulated data class or jurisdiction mismatch. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise.
conditions: IF regulated data from Plane is sent through Plano to a non-approved external API
IF Plano logs retain Plane-derived content beyond policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Plane uploads
Disable or minimize Plano request logging
Confirm vendor DPAs before routing data
Use separate retention settings for each system
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing controls
